candidates: When adding a temperature parameter to any new MD dynamics class in `ase/md/`, name it `temperature_K` to stay consistent with the convention used by `Langevin`, `VelocityVerlet`, `NVTBerendsen`, and `NPTBerendsen`.
Don't use the `if param is None: param = default` pattern for new parameters that have no backward-compatibility requirement; declare them as normal required positional arguments.

Don't override `todict()` in new MD subclasses unless there is a clear, documented serialization purpose. If you do override it, ensure every dictionary key matches the exact corresponding `__init__` parameter name (e.g. use `'fixcm'` not `'fix-cm'`, `'temperature_K'` not `'temperature_eV'`).
When implementing Box-Muller or other log-based transforms on uniform random samples, use `log(1 - y)` rather than `log(y)` to avoid a domain error when the sampled value is exactly 0.

New MD thermostat implementations must include a test (or a linked open issue) that verifies RATTLE constraints are preserved during and after thermalization — e.g. check that constrained DOFs remain constrained and that average kinetic energy reflects the reduced DOF count.
Name the center-of-mass fixing attribute `fix_com` (not `fixcm`) in MD classes, following the prior art in `ase/atoms.py`.
In MD `step()` method signatures and bodies, name the forces variable `forces` rather than `f` so it is greppable across the codebase.

In numerical methods within MD classes, use numpy array math instead of Python loops — e.g. generate all random velocities with a single vectorized call and apply conditional velocity replacement with boolean array indexing.

Related MD tests (for `VelocityVerlet`, `Langevin`, `Andersen`, etc.) must share setup code via common helper functions, pytest fixtures, or `@pytest.mark.parametrize`; never copy-paste test setup or assertion logic across test files.

When a test condition can be verified in one or a few MD steps (e.g. demonstrating that a thermostat with probability/friction set to zero reproduces `VelocityVerlet`), use the minimum number of steps required; do not run a long trajectory to check what a single step can verify.

In MD classes that generate per-atom random data, store those arrays as instance attributes and broadcast them via `self.communicator` before use, so parallel runs under gpaw or asap3 keep all MPI tasks synchronized.

When `communicator=None` is passed to an MD class constructor, replace it immediately with `DummyMPI()` in `__init__` rather than sprinkling `if self.communicator is not None:` guards throughout `step()`. This keeps `step()` clean and matches the pattern now used by both `Langevin` and `Andersen`.

Common logic shared across MD subclasses — such as center-of-mass velocity (`_get_com_velocity`), center-of-mass position correction, or momentum adjustment — must live in `MolecularDynamics` in `ase/md/md.py` rather than being duplicated in each subclass.

Temperature assertions in MD tests must use tight quantitative bounds justified by a controlled RNG seed (e.g., `|avg_temp - 300| < 10 K` over a long trajectory). Loose sanity-check ranges such as `T > 50 and T < 1000` are not meaningful and should be removed; rely on the longer-trajectory asap3-backed tests instead.

New functionality for `ase/atoms.py` that extends existing behavior (e.g. moving atoms to a specific center-of-mass position) should be expressed as a new keyword argument on an existing method such as `atoms.center()`, not as an entirely new standalone method, in order to keep the `Atoms` API coherent.

Don't add inline comments that merely restate what the adjacent docstring or the code itself already makes clear; reserve inline comments for non-obvious logic, side-effects, or project-specific invariants.
